title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 437
paragraphs: Now Amasis, as one may suppose, did not fail to notice that Polycrates was enjoying extraordinary good fortune, and this was a matter of concern to him. And as still more good fortune continued to come to Polycrates, he wrote these words upon a paper and sent it to Samos: “Amasis to Polycrates says this: It is a pleasant thing to hear that a friend and guest is faring well; yet your great good fortune is not pleasing to me, since I know that the Divinity is jealous. I desire, both for myself and for those I care about, that in some of our affairs we should prosper and in others should fail, and so go through life alternately faring well and ill, rather than be prosperous in all things. For I have never yet heard tell of anyone who was prosperous in all things and did not come to an utterly evil end at last. Now therefore, follow my counsel and act as I shall say regarding your prosperous fortunes. Think carefully, and whatever you find to be the most valued by you — that for the loss of which you would most be vexed in your soul — take that and cast it away in such a manner that it will never again come into the sight of men; and if hereafter good fortune does not befall you in alternation with calamities, apply remedies in the way I have suggested.”
